title: Handoff Communique and Ops Synthetic Log — 2028-11-02
content:
TL;DR:
- Quietish week with two noisy spikes: a short KV-cache degradation (impact: regressions in streaming latencies), and a cross-region DNS flapping event affecting private deployments in eu-west-1 for ~22m.
- SLOs: tail latency SLO nudged close to threshold during cache regressions; error budget burn increased ~1.8% this week.
- Handovers: added a short checklist for warm vs cold KV cache warms; oncall-to-oncall had a missing context link (fixed).

Notes and run-of-show (chronological):
2028-10-28 02:14 UTC — KV-cache degradation (INC-OPS-2028-10-28-KV):
- Symptom: increased p99 generation latency for hosted-api model endpoints, streaming stalls, multiple user reports.
- Detection: synthetic streaming probes detected 350ms+ spikes (baseline ~60ms). Alert routed to SRE oncall.
- Immediate mitigations: rolled forward emergency canary to bypass hot cache layer for affected model family, temporarily increased batching window for GPUs servicing that shard, rotated a failing cache node.
- Root cause (quick summary): a background compaction job caused a short GC/IO pressure window on the NVMe-backed KV nodes; this surfaced at peak segment merging times and coincided with a shift in request shape (higher short-sequence traffic).
- User-visible impact: increased latency and a handful of rate-limit escalations; no data loss.
- Next steps: (1) throttle compaction during the 01:00–05:00 UTC maintenance window; (2) make compaction lower-priority on NVMe pool; (3) add observable to detect compaction-IO spikes and tie into autoscaling rules. Owner: Jasper. ETA: 2028-11-10.

2028-10-30 18:43 UTC — DNS flapping in eu-west-1 private control plane (INC-OPS-2028-10-30-DNS):
- Symptom: periodic failures to reach private-control-plane endpoints for customers with VPC routing; transient 504s.
- Detection: customer support ticket + internal ping monitors triggered; span-level traces show TCP connect resets.
- Immediate mitigations: switched affected routes to route-policy "fallback-region"; engaged network infra to investigate BGP announcements between partner colos.
- Root cause: misconfiguration in an upstream colo pair causing rapid withdraw/announce; amplification due to aggressive DNS TTLs for the control-plane zone.
- Customer impact: ~22 minutes of synthetic failures for 18 customers, several support escalation threads.
- Next steps: (1) coordinate with partner to correct peering configuration; (2) lower DNS TTL for control-plane to 30s for rapid failover; (3) add automatic fallback rule to route policy for private deployments. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2028-11-07.

SLOs & Signals (current):
- Generation p99 (hosted-api): 98.6% within SLO (target 99.5%). Trend: -0.7% week-over-week.
- Error budget burn (monthly): consumed 6.4% YTD for November window; this week added ~1.8%.
- Embeddings throughput (dedicated): avg latency 42ms (SLO 50ms) — healthy.
- Incidents this week contributed primarily to tail latency; no durability SLOs were impacted.

On-call Handoff (this rotation):
- Outgoing: Liam O'Connor (night shift) — left the following actionable items in the handoff doc:
  * Note: watch KV compaction job schedules (compaction-engine v2.3.1). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-compaction-runbook
  * Open PR: serving-runtime PR #782 contains a mitigation to lower GC pressure on cache worker replicas. Reviewer: Jasper.
- Incoming: Ruth Delgado (day shift) — please verify the compaction throttle is applied before peak window and confirm autoscaling hook behaves as expected.
- Handoff checklist additions (new):
  1) Confirm synthetic streaming probe thresholds (p99/p999) are healthy for all model families.
  2) Verify fallback-route-policy is active for any private-control-plane route with ttl < 60s.
  3) Check latest support tickets flagged critical and mark follow-ups.

Runbook & Playbook updates made this week:
- Added a short appendix to the KV cache playbook describing compaction backoff and how to temporarily bypass hot shards. Author: Jasper.
- DNS failover playbook: added a quick run-down for partner peering contacts and a template support message for customers. Author: Priya.
- Small editorial note: standardize "fallback-region" policy name across docs and code (task created). Owner: Ava. ETA: 2028-11-08.

Capacity & Ops Planning:
- Autoscaling: autoscaler observed a 9% uplift during a batch job ramp in the Dedicated pool; no scaling failures but headroom briefly dropped below 12%. Action: increase base pool for dedicated-gpu-a from 6->8 for peak windows. Owner: Ops infra (Charlie) — planning ticket OPS-2189.
- Forecast: expected 12% monthly growth in inference requests for December (seasonal holiday traffic in EU). Consider prewarming an extra shard for eur-1 region in late November.

Action Items (short):
- Jasper: implement compaction throttling and add IO spike alert. Due 2028-11-10.
- Priya: coordinate with partner to fix BGP peering and lower TTL for control-plane. Due 2028-11-07.
- Ava: rename fallback policy references across docs + code; add a short confluence page with examples. Due 2028-11-08.
- Ruth: validate warm cache playbook during next oncall drill (2028-11-06).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we expose compaction schedule tuning to customers on Dedicated? Tradeoffs: transparency vs accidental self-inflicted outages.
- Consider a small feature: synthetic warmup traffic for newly provisioned shards — would reduce cold-start tail but increase churn/cost. Worth a pilot?
- Postmortem plan: decide whether to elevate KV-cache incident to full RCA postmortem (recommended) — if yes, schedule RCA readout with Applied ML and Serving Runtime next week.

Miscellaneous / quick links:
- Incidents: https://ops.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-10-28-kv, https://ops.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-10-30-dns
- Playbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-cache-playbook, https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/dns-failover
- Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/782

Meeting notes / standing items for next week:
- Mon 2028-11-05 (09:00 PT) — Reliability sync: include Applied ML to discuss cache access patterns. Owner: Ava.
- Wed 2028-11-07 (15:00 UTC) — Incident review: DNS flapping post-incident call; invite network infra and partner ops. Owner: Priya.
- Fri 2028-11-09 (11:00 PT) — Oncall drill & runbook walkthrough. Owner: Ruth.

Closing:
- Tone: manageable; operational debt highlighted around compaction tuning and defensive DNS TTLing. Focus for the week: reduce tail latencies and harden private control-plane routing.

Notes to self (unpolished):
- remember to push small note about "fallback-region" naming into SDK config docs too.
- check with billing if we need to adjust cost attribution for pre-warm shards before approving capacity increase.
